pull.title: disputes: adjudicate receipt-backed expenses independently
pull.body:
## Summary
- add optional `approvedExpenseAmount` to admin dispute resolution
- allow labor escrow outcome and verified expense reimbursement to be decided independently
- reimburse only the approved portion of submitted claims and refund the rest of the expense budget
- reject expense settlement when resuming a job
- preserve backward-compatible behavior when the new field is omitted
- add regression coverage for partial expense approval and over-approval prevention
- document the financial and audit semantics

## Why
The expense escrow introduced for real purchases was still all-or-nothing during disputes. A job can legitimately require refunding the service price while still reimbursing verified materials, or releasing service compensation while rejecting part of the receipt evidence. Treating those money components independently is necessary for commercially correct dispute handling.

## Migration
No Flyway migration is required. The existing V42 expense escrow already persists final reimbursed/refunded totals and enforces conservation of funds.

## Validation
Do not merge until every required workflow/check for the exact latest head is complete and green. Fix failures on this branch and rerun before merge.

issue.title: web: expose expense adjudication in admin disputes
issue.body:
## Summary
- wire `approvedExpenseAmount` through the admin dispute API client
- add an explicit expense adjudication control to the admin dispute resolution form
- preserve backward-compatible default settlement semantics when no exact amount is selected
- block expense adjudication entirely for `RESUME_JOB`
- validate non-negative PLN amounts with cent precision before submission
- explain that any unapproved part of the expense budget returns to the requester

## Why
#111 made labor compensation and receipt-backed expense reimbursement independently adjudicable in the backend. Without an admin UI, that production capability was not operationally usable. This slice exposes it without changing the existing default behavior for disputes that do not need partial expense decisions.

## Migration
No Flyway migration is required; this consumes the API contract introduced by #111.

## Validation
Do not merge until every required latest-head workflow/check is complete and green.
